newsitem.title: BELGIUM: GAN BELGIUM DOES NOT SEE RB/AXA BELGIUM TOGETHER.
newsitem.headline: GAN BELGIUM DOES NOT SEE RB/AXA BELGIUM TOGETHER.

text.p: GAN Belgium Chairman Louis Durieux said on Friday he believed Royale Belge and AXA Belgium could not continue to co-exist separately within the AXA-UAP group.

"Between AXA Belgium and Royale Belge there are conflicts every day in commercial terms and it's not possible to continue like that," he told a news conference on 1996 results of GAN Belgium, a unit of Swiss Life .
Durieux is also head of Swiss Life Belgium, which bought GAN last year from its French parent GAN for 3.5 billion Belgian francs.
There is growing speculation that AXA-UAP is studying the sale of one of its Belgian units, having ruled out a merger because of the damage this would do to its network of Belgian brokers and agents.
Le Monde newspaper reported two weeks ago that Royale Belge was about to be sold either to Dutch group ING or Switzerland's Winterthur . Winterthur denied the rumour.
"ING was interested in (GAN Belgium) but I don't know if this is a sign of their interest in Belgium," GAN Belgium chief executive officer Jacques Vanhee said.
